clue.text: Wearing short pants, work for very little money

indicators.note: the trousers are worn around the work, so one piece sits inside the other
short says the word for pants loses its final letter

parts.note: KECKS is British slang for trousers or pants
OP is the usual abbreviation for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone takes a menial job in skimpy shorts for a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: Kecks is British slang for trousers; 'short' docks its last letter, and 'Wearing' means the trousers go round the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A kopeck is a Russian coin worth one hundredth of a rouble, a tiny sum.

clue.text: Skilful feat by skier, getting boot to fit

parts.note: to boot something is to kick it
a turn is a sudden fit or attack, as in giving someone a turn

explanation.surface: A skier performs a stunt after squeezing a foot into a boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' and 'fit' seem to be about ski boots fitting; they are a verb for kicking and a sudden attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick turn is a standing ski manoeuvre, swinging one ski round to face the other way.

clue.text: Held up first prize

indicators.note: in a down light, held up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: First prize is lifted aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a sum of money or trophy to be won, so it means a prize.

clue.text: Warm drink in my mug

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
dial and mug are both slang for the face

explanation.surface: A hot drink in a favourite cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' is a second definition, a cordial being a sweet drink; 'COR!' is British slang for 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly, as in a cordial welcome.

clue.text: Prevented current measure being adopted by hospital department head

indicators.note: a piece adopted by others is taken in among them, so it goes inside
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the ampere is the unit measuring electric current

explanation.surface: A hospital department head blocks a new way of measuring current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hospital department head' reads as one official, but it is H plus the first letter of 'department', with AMPERE taken in between.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to hinder or obstruct them, so hampered is a synonym of prevented.

clue.text: Store's entire management is disorganised

definitions.meaning: running everything in a shop, from one end to the other
scattered everywhere in a chaotic way

explanation.surface: A shop's whole management team is in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means in complete disorder, scattered everywhere; literally it could mean covering every part of a store.

clue.text: Model Spanish kingdom once put under pressure

indicators.note: in a down light the kingdom is placed below the pressure letter

parts.note: Aragon was a medieval kingdom of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: An old Spanish realm was pushed into becoming an exemplar.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of a quality.

clue.text: Half one country's population in crammed housing given new lease of life?

indicators.note: the crammed word houses the half nationality inside itself

parts.note: to cram is to revise intensively for an exam

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for the nation's people is kept

parts.note: Italians are the population of Italy

explanation.surface: Half a nation's people live in packed homes that have been renovated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crammed housing' looks like overcrowded homes, but 'crammed' means studied hard for an exam and 'housing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To revitalise is to restore energy and vigour, giving something a new lease of life.

clue.text: Con and Lab fiddling expenses, initially easy to achieve

parts.note: to do someone is to con them

indicators.note: fiddling, as with accounts, says the letters are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Tory and Labour MPs fiddle expenses since it is easily done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con and Lab' look like the two parties; 'Con' is DO (cheat), 'fiddling' turns LAB into ABL, and E comes from 'expenses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doable is achievable without great difficulty, feasible.

clue.text: Sailors from Plymouth left before dark in ship after storms

indicators.note: the left and dark pieces go inside the shuffled letters
storms makes the letters rage and fall into disorder
before places the left letter ahead of the dark word

parts.note: grim means dark or gloomy

explanation.surface: Seamen set sail from Plymouth before dark, their ship battered by storms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' scrambles the ship and after letters into PIFATHERS, split to take the left-and-dark piece. The Mayflower pilgrims sailed from Plymouth in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers were the English settlers who sailed from Plymouth on the Mayflower in 1620.

clue.text: I will come in to provide standard sort of grub

parts.note: to cater is to provide food or what is needed

indicators.note: the contracted words come in, entering the middle of the next piece

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
I'LL is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: A promise to come in and supply a decent standard of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food, matching 'provide'; here it is the larva sense, and the answer is a kind of grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub can mean an insect larva, and a caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly or moth.

clue.text: Compete no end against ace, getting through

indicators.note: no end says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to vie is to compete
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A contest against a top player, with a player getting past.
explanation.definitionFit: Via is a preposition meaning by way of, so it can replace through as in travelling via Paris.

clue.text: Evidence of clock going and stopping after losing seconds

indicators.note: after losing says a letter is dropped from the word for stopping

parts.note: sticking, as a jammed mechanism does, means stopping

explanation.surface: A clock seems to be running, then halts once the seconds are lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticking sound is the audible sign that a clock's mechanism is working.

clue.text: Domestic animals linked in one sort of story one wouldn't buy?

definitions.text: one sort of story one wouldn't buy?

parts.note: a cockerel, a farmyard creature
and is the word that links two things
a bull, another farmyard creature

explanation.surface: Farm animals feature in an unbelievable tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buy' is the slang sense of believe, so the story is one nobody accepts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock-and-bull story is an absurd, implausible tale nobody would believe.

clue.text: Herbs are great, used in regular amounts for stuffing meat

indicators.note: the picked letters serve to stuff the meat, so they go inside it

parts.note: veal is the meat of a calf

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word is used, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A cook praises herbs, measured out evenly as stuffing for meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'great' give GET, which stuffs VEAL. The definition is 'Herbs are': herbs are vegetal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetal means belonging to plants, so it completes a sentence describing herbs as plant life.

clue.text: Defiantly organised, a cleric at length's imprisoned by ghastly tyrant

indicators.note: organised says the letters of the first words are set in a new order
the length is shut up inside the tyrant's letters
ghastly says the letters of the tyrant are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A churchman held at length by a dreadful despot is arranged to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the first words into RECALCI; 'ghastly' gives TRANTY, which imprisons L to make TRANTLY. 'at' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalcitrant means obstinately uncooperative, so the adverb describes acting in defiance.

clue.text: Alienate group of forest rangers

indicators.note: group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Turn a team of woodland wardens against you.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to make them hostile or distant, to alienate them.

clue.text: Among items on sale, easy to get horse in exchange? Not for Richard, in these

indicators.note: the easy piece and the shuffled horse go among the goods, inside them

parts.note: wares are goods offered for sale
soft means easy, as in a soft option

indicators.note: in exchange says the letters of the animal are swapped about

explanation.surface: At a market a horse is easy to swap, unlike for Richard III, who offered his kingdom for one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in exchange' scrambles the horse into HEROS. Shakespeare's Richard III cries 'my kingdom for a horse' at Bosworth, the last battle of these English civil wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century civil wars between York and Lancaster ended with Richard III killed at Bosworth.

clue.text: Scrubber is more confident around company

indicators.note: around says the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: surer means more certain or confident

explanation.surface: A cleaner grows more self-assured in company.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourer is a pad used for scrubbing pans clean.

clue.text: German runner's injured her shin

definitions.note: of the Rhine, a German river; in crosswords a runner can be a river

indicators.note: injured says the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A German athlete has hurt her shin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; it is a river, the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish means relating to the Rhine, a river that runs through Germany.

clue.text: Father: one's ultimate buddy?

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
I is the Roman numeral one
the end is the ultimate or final thing

explanation.surface: Dad is someone's best mate in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A buddy is an informal word for a pal or close companion.

clue.text: Survive speaker's mocking scepticism

indicators.note: speaker's says the words are as they are said aloud, not as written

parts.note: to ride someone is to tease or mock them; doubt is scepticism

explanation.surface: Someone weathers a public figure's derisive disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, the D at the end of 'ride' merges with the D at the start of 'doubt', which leaves 'ride out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride out a storm or crisis is to come through it safely, to survive it.

clue.text: Poet and writer held by communists in revolution

indicators.note: the writer is held inside the communists
revolution turns the word round so that it reads backwards

parts.note: Reds is the usual name for communists
a pen is a writing instrument, a writer

explanation.surface: A poet and author are detained by communists during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' gives SDER. Stephen Spender was a 20th-century English poet, leftist in the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was a leading English poet of the 1930s, once leftist like the communists in the surface.

clue.text: In Europe see first appearance of migratory bird

indicators.note: the picked letter goes in the abbreviation for Europe

parts.note: EU is the European Union, standing for Europe

indicators.note: the first letter to appear in the word is the one wanted

explanation.surface: In Europe you can watch the first arrival of migrating birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'migratory bird' wants to be one definition, but the emu does not migrate: M goes in EU, and 'see' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Speaker's right to hate ironic raving

indicators.note: raving, wild and incoherent, says the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An orator is entitled to loathe wild sarcasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's' is 'Speaker is', the 's being a link; 'raving' scrambles HATE IRONIC into HETORICIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorician is a skilled public orator, someone who makes speeches.

clue.text: One bridge player holding clubs and diamonds

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
E is East, one of the four players at a bridge table

explanation.surface: A card player holds both clubs and diamonds in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' seems to be another suit next to 'clubs', but it is the definition: ICE is slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, from their glittering, icy look.

clue.text: Daughter's given sweet sherry, sadly

parts.note: oloroso is a dark, often sweetened, style of sherry

explanation.surface: A daughter is mournfully handed a glass of sweet sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition, a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Doloroso is the musical direction asking for a sorrowful, plaintive performance.

clue.text: Observe husband going back into church in Lancashire, perhaps

indicators.note: the husband and the reversed word go into the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: going back says the word reads in the opposite direction

parts.note: to see is to observe

explanation.surface: A husband is seen returning to a Lancashire church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns SEE into EES. 'Lancashire' seems to be a county but is a crumbly British cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a crumbly English cheese named after the county, an example of the category.
